calcium-activated calcineurin significantly reduces the in vitro and in vivo sensitivity of C. albicans to FLC through Rta2p.
calcium-activated-calineurin reduces the in vitro and in vivo sensitivity of FLC to C. albicans through Rta2p.
calcium-activated- calcineurin, via Rta2, reduces the sensitivity of Candida albicans to the first-line drug fluconazole.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of calcineurin and RTA2 in the regulation of the antifungal efficacy of FLC and provides a new strategy for the treatment of systemic candidiasia.
the molecular basis of FLC resistance in C. albican and provides a potential target for new antifungal drug development.
the molecular basis of the calcineurins-mediated resistance to FCL in C. albican.

calcium-activated calcineurin, via Rta2, is a critical regulator of the efficacy of FCL against candidemia.
